guide.title: How to read this report
guide.intro: The pilot report checks whether Tanbeeh does its job at each restaurant: customers are told when their order is ready, and they come to collect it. Figures come from the daily roll-up, so today can be incomplete.

tickets.text: Order numbers created in the date range, whether by staff, the POS or the API.

ready.text: Tickets staff marked ready at least once. Every percentage below is out of this number.

reach.text: Share of ready tickets where the customer could be alerted: a push notification was sent to their phone, or their order page was open. The rest had the page closed with no push, or no phone following. This is the main health figure: aim high.

acknowledged.text: Share of ready tickets where the customer tapped to confirm they saw the alert. It shows real attention; customers who simply walk up do not tap, so it is always lower than reach.

prep.text: Time from ticket creation to marked ready. The median is the typical order; the 90th percentile is the slow end: 9 in 10 orders were faster.

pickup.text: Time from ready to collected. Short times mean the alerts bring people to the counter.

uncollected.text: Tickets marked ready that expired without being collected. A high count points to customers who were not reached or left.

undo.text: Share of ready tickets staff moved back, usually a mistap. A high value means staff need help with the board.

guide.tip: Compare restaurants over the same range. Low reach with many uncollected tickets usually means customers are not keeping the order page open or allowing notifications: ask the restaurant to show the QR poster and the "keep this page open" hint at the counter.
